title: 8-bit Quantization Provides No Privacy Benefit Against Training-Free Embedding Inversion

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to enable a fair comparison of quantization's privacy benefit by controlling for confounding retrieval-utility differences. Paper [12] discusses the privacy implications of quantization in networked control systems, identifying a trade-off between control performance and privacy. However, it does not address the specific objective of controlling for retrieval-utility differences to enable fair privacy comparisons. Paper [18] explores privacy-utility tradeoffs but focuses on constrained data release mechanisms rather than quantization or embedding inversion. No prior paper explicitly targets the same purpose of fair privacy comparison by controlling retrieval utility differences.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism involves calibrating a Gaussian noise baseline to match 8-bit quantization's retrieval utility, then attacking both with ZSInvert, a training-free LLM-based embedding inversion. Paper [24] revisits the Gaussian mechanism for differential privacy, providing analytical calibration methods, but does not match quantization's retrieval utility or involve embedding inversion. Paper [19] uses masked diffusion models for embedding inversion but does not involve Gaussian noise calibration or quantization. Paper [17] proposes BeamClean for embedding inversion but does not address Gaussian noise calibration or utility matching. No prior paper combines Gaussian noise calibration with embedding inversion in this manner.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses a utility-matched protocol anchored at nDCG@10 approximately 0.544 for both defenses. Paper [20] critiques privacy evaluations but does not use utility-matched protocols or nDCG@10. Paper [15] evaluates embedding inversion but does not use utility-matched protocols or nDCG@10. Paper [26] evaluates defenses against embedding inversion but does not use utility-matched protocols or nDCG@10. No prior paper employs the same evaluation design.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of text-embedding privacy and inversion attacks. Paper [1] investigates privacy risks in text embeddings, focusing on transfer attacks. Paper [5] studies embedding inversion as a privacy risk in NLP and security. Paper [15] explores embedding inversion attacks in dense retrieval systems. Paper [26] defends against embedding inversion attacks in LLM embeddings. All these papers address text-embedding privacy and inversion attacks, covering the domain.

These papers focus on privacy risks, embedding inversion attacks, and defenses in the context of text embeddings.
